scenario: 广告 CTR 系统：100K QPS、10ms SLA。有人默认「要么上 transformer 要么落伍」。
scenario_en: An ad CTR system at 100K QPS, 10ms SLA; someone assumes 'use a transformer or fall behind.'
q: 在这种高吞吐/严延迟系统里，该怎么看待 LR 和 GBDT？
q_en: How should you regard LR and GBDT in such a high-throughput, tight-latency system?
why: 把 LR/GBDT 当生产级系统，不是过渡的踏脚石。当延迟、吞吐、成本主导时，transformer 常是错误默认——LR/GBDT 往往才是对的设计。用量化的取舍来辩护，而不是靠「更先进」。
why_en: Treat LR/GBDT as production-grade systems, not stepping stones; when latency, throughput, and cost dominate, a transformer is usually the wrong default.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  R["需求: 100K QPS / 10ms"] --> C["LR / GBDT 生产级"]
  C -.升级触发.-> N["非结构化/需共享embedding → 神经"]
options: 它们只是过渡踏脚石，正式系统迟早要全部换成 transformer
把 LR/GBDT 当生产级方案，延迟/吞吐/成本主导时它们才是对的设计
高 QPS 系统只能上最复杂的模型，经典模型在 100K QPS 下必然扛不住
选哪个纯看精度排行榜，延迟和成本等上线之后再慢慢优化
options_en: They're only stepping stones; a real system eventually has to switch everything to a transformer.
Treat LR/GBDT as production-grade: when latency, throughput and cost dominate they're the right design.
High-QPS systems can only run the most complex model; classical models will buckle at 100K QPS.
Pick purely off an accuracy leaderboard and tune latency and cost after launch.
optionExplanations: 「踏脚石」心态正是要破的误区：良好工程化的 LR 可匹敌复杂替代，是正经生产方案。
对；高吞吐+严延迟下 LR/GBDT 常胜，关键是用量化取舍（0.1ms、KB 模型）来辩护。
恰恰相反：复杂模型延迟高，100K QPS/10ms 下先被排除，经典模型才扛得住。
只看精度榜会忽略 10ms SLA 与成本，规模化上根本落不了地。
optionExplanations_en: The 'stepping stone' mindset is the fallacy to break: well-engineered LR rivals complex alternatives and is a real production choice.
Correct — under high throughput and tight latency LR/GBDT often win, defended by quantified trade-offs (0.1ms, KB model).
The opposite: complex models are high-latency and get ruled out first at 100K QPS/10ms; classical copes.
An accuracy-only view ignores the 10ms SLA and cost and can't ship at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量系统吞吐；100K QPS 是高吞吐场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures throughput; 100K QPS is a high-throughput scenario.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树（XGBoost/LightGBM），表格数据的生产级高效模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees, e.g. XGBoost/LightGBM) is a production-grade, efficient model for tabular data.

scenario: 你要向面试官说清逻辑回归为什么能做到亚毫秒推理。
scenario_en: You explain to the interviewer why logistic regression achieves sub-millisecond inference.
q: 逻辑回归单次预测的计算量是什么级别？
q_en: What's the compute cost of one logistic-regression prediction?
why: 一次预测 = 一个点积加 sigmoid：ŷ = σ(wᵀx + b)。在单个 CPU 核上就是亚毫秒。计算量只随特征数线性增长，没有矩阵层叠或注意力，所以极快、可确定性复现。
why_en: One prediction is a single dot product plus a sigmoid, ŷ = σ(wᵀx + b), sub-ms on one CPU core because cost grows only linearly in features.
codeSample:
# 逻辑回归推理 = 一个点积 + sigmoid
z = np.dot(w, x) + b        # 权重·特征，O(特征数)
y_hat = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z)) # sigmoid 压到 (0,1) 概率
# 单 CPU 核 ~0.1ms；无矩阵层叠、无注意力
options: 需要多层矩阵乘法和注意力计算，延迟和同规模 DNN 相当
一个点积加 sigmoid，单 CPU 核亚毫秒，随特征数线性增长
每次预测都要遍历一棵决策树的全部分裂节点才能出结果
必须有 GPU 才算得动，纯 CPU 环境下根本跑不起来
options_en: It needs multi-layer matrix multiplies and attention, with latency like a DNN of the same size.
One dot product plus a sigmoid — sub-millisecond on a single CPU core, linear in feature count.
Every prediction has to walk all the split nodes of a decision tree before it returns.
It needs a GPU to compute and simply won't run on a CPU-only box.
optionExplanations: LR 没有矩阵层叠或注意力，说延迟与 DNN 相当完全不符。
对；点积+sigmoid 是 O(特征数) 的单次运算，这就是它亚毫秒、可复现的根源。
遍历分裂节点是决策树/GBDT 的推理方式，不是 LR。
LR 在 CPU 上就极快，根本不需要 GPU。
optionExplanations_en: LR has no stacked matmuls or attention, so 'DNN-level latency' is entirely wrong.
Correct — a dot product + sigmoid is one O(features) operation, the source of its sub-ms, reproducible speed.
Traversing split nodes is how decision trees/GBDT infer, not LR.
LR is extremely fast on CPU and needs no GPU at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把实数压到 (0,1) 的函数 σ(z)=1/(1+e^-z)，LR 用它输出概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sigmoid σ(z)=1/(1+e^-z) squashes a real number into (0,1); LR uses it to output a probability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 权重向量与特征向量对应相乘再求和，O(特征数) 的运算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dot product multiplies weights by features elementwise and sums, an O(features) operation.

scenario: 广告竞价的端到端预算是 10ms，里面还要留给网络往返、特征取数、拍卖逻辑。LR 推理约 0.1ms（CPU）。
scenario_en: The ad-auction end-to-end budget is 10ms, also covering network hops, feature retrieval, and auction logic. LR inference is ~0.1ms (CPU).
q: LR 的 0.1ms 推理对 10ms 预算意味着什么？
q_en: What does LR's 0.1ms inference mean for the 10ms budget?
why: LR 推理只吃掉 10ms 里的约 0.1ms（1%），剩下 ~9.9ms 全留给网络往返、特征取数、拍卖逻辑。这正是面试要的量化——把模型延迟摆进整个预算里，说明它几乎不占预算，所以能进这条严格路径。
why_en: LR eats ~0.1ms (1%) of the 10ms, leaving ~9.9ms for network hops, feature retrieval, and auction logic — a quantified fit into the budget.
options: LR 推理会吃掉 10ms 里的绝大部分，其它环节几乎没时间了
只占约 0.1ms（1%），剩 ~9.9ms 留给网络、取特征和拍卖逻辑
0.1ms 只是随手估的数字，对预算怎么分配没有实际参考意义
延迟只需看模型本身，网络往返和特征取数不算进这 10ms
options_en: LR inference eats almost the whole 10ms and leaves nearly nothing for the other steps.
It takes about 0.1ms (1%), leaving ~9.9ms for network, feature fetch and auction logic.
0.1ms is just a made-up figure and tells you nothing about how to split the budget.
Latency is only about the model; network round trips and feature fetches don't count.
optionExplanations: 0.1ms 只占 10ms 的 1%，说它吃掉整个预算与量级不符。
对；把 0.1ms 摆进 10ms 预算，剩 9.9ms 给其它环节，这种量化正是面试加分点。
0.1ms 是可解释的量级锚点，直接决定还剩多少预算，非常有意义。
10ms 是端到端预算，网络/特征取数/拍卖都在里面，不能只算模型。
optionExplanations_en: 0.1ms is only 1% of 10ms, so 'eats the whole budget' is off by magnitudes.
Correct — placing 0.1ms into the 10ms budget leaves 9.9ms for other steps; that quantification is what scores.
0.1ms is an explainable anchor that directly sets how much budget remains — very meaningful.
10ms is the end-to-end budget covering network/feature retrieval/auction, not just the model.

termDefinitions.term: end-to-end latency budget / 端到端延迟预算
termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求全链路可用的总时间（10ms），模型推理只占其中一段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The end-to-end latency budget is the total time per request (10ms), of which model inference is one slice.

scenario: 你要把 CTR 模型部署到成千上万个节点甚至边缘设备，每个副本都要加载模型。
scenario_en: You deploy the CTR model to thousands of nodes, even edge devices, each replica loading the model.
q: 怎么让线性模型小到能轻松铺满上万节点？
q_en: How do you make a linear model small enough to blanket thousands of nodes?
why: 用 L1 正则把大量权重压成 0（稀疏化），序列化后的模型只有 KB 级，加载/分发极轻，可轻松铺到上万节点甚至边缘。L1 的稀疏性直接换来更小的服务体积。
why_en: L1 regularization zeros out many weights (sparsity), so the serialized model is kilobytes and deploys trivially to thousands of nodes or the edge.
tradeoff: L1 稀疏（模型 KB、易分发，但可能丢弱相关特征） vs 稠密权重（保留全部特征但模型更大）
options: 用 L2 正则把所有权重都放大，模型体积自然就跟着变小
用 L1 正则把大量权重压成 0，序列化后只有 KB 级
把模型常驻 GPU 显存里，节点数量就不再受模型体积限制
多加特征让模型更丰富，体积对铺开部署本来就没影响
options_en: Use L2 to blow all the weights up, and the model naturally gets smaller.
Use L1 to drive many weights to zero, so the serialized model is only kilobytes.
Keep the model resident in GPU memory so node count stops being limited by size.
Add more features for richness; size never affects how widely you can deploy.
optionExplanations: L2 只把权重收缩变小、不置零，不产生稀疏，压不小模型体积。
对；L1 制造稀疏、把无用权重清零，模型 KB 级，分发到上万节点几乎无成本。
放显存不减小模型本身，且边缘设备未必有 GPU，思路跑偏。
加特征反而变大，忽视体积会让分发到上万节点变得昂贵。
optionExplanations_en: L2 shrinks weights toward zero without zeroing them, producing no sparsity, so it can't shrink model size.
Correct — L1 creates sparsity by zeroing useless weights, yielding a KB model that deploys to thousands of nodes at near-zero cost.
GPU memory doesn't shrink the model itself, and edge devices may lack GPUs — off track.
Adding features enlarges the model; ignoring size makes fan-out to thousands of nodes costly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对权重绝对值惩罚，会把不重要的权重压成 0，产生稀疏模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L1 regularization penalizes absolute weights and drives unimportant ones to zero, yielding a sparse model.

scenario: 面试官问：用 LR 做 CTR，性能提升主要靠调架构还是靠别的？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: with LR for CTR, do gains come from tuning the architecture or something else?
q: 用 LR 做 CTR 时，投入主要该花在哪？
q_en: With LR for CTR, where does the investment go?
why: 投入在特征工程而非架构：hashed 特征交叉（user ID × ad category 压成一个稀疏特征）、频率编码、以及校准过的概率。LR 的架构极简，性能靠喂给它的特征——特征管线才是主战场。
why_en: The investment is feature engineering, not architecture: hashed feature crosses, frequency encodings, and calibrated probabilities.
options: 花在调网络层数、激活函数和优化器超参这类架构搜索上
花在特征工程：hashed 特征交叉、频率编码、概率校准
花在挑选更高端的 GPU 型号和更大的显存容量上
花在把 LR 换成更深的模型上，特征管线保持原样
options_en: On architecture search — layer counts, activation functions, optimizer hyperparameters.
On feature engineering: hashed feature crosses, frequency encodings, calibrated probabilities.
On picking a higher-end GPU with more memory.
On swapping LR for a deeper model while leaving the feature pipeline alone.
optionExplanations: LR 没有网络层数和激活可调，调架构无从谈起。
对；LR 架构固定，收益全来自特征——交叉、编码、校准是投入的重点。
LR 在 CPU 上跑，选 GPU 型号与它的性能无关。
换深模型是另起炉灶，题目问的是「用 LR 时」投入花在哪。
optionExplanations_en: LR has no layer count or activations to tune, so 'tuning architecture' doesn't apply.
Correct — LR's architecture is fixed; gains come entirely from features — crosses, encodings, calibration are the focus.
LR runs on CPU, so GPU model choice is irrelevant to its performance.
Switching to a deep model is a different approach; the question is where investment goes 'when using LR.'

termDefinitions.term: hashed feature cross / 哈希特征交叉
termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个特征组合（如 userID×adCategory）哈希成一个稀疏特征，捕捉交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hashed feature cross combines two features (e.g. userID×adCategory) hashed into one sparse feature to capture interaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用类别出现频率替代类别本身作为数值特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Frequency encoding replaces a category with its occurrence frequency as a numeric feature.

scenario: 广告用 generalized second-price（GSP）拍卖，直接拿模型输出的 P(click) 乘出价算期望收益来排序。模型 A 排序 AUC 很高，但输出的 P(click)=0.03 实际点击率只有 0.5%。
scenario_en: Ads use a generalized second-price (GSP) auction, ranking by P(click)×bid for expected revenue. Model A has high ranking AUC but its P(click)=0.03 corresponds to a real 0.5% click rate.
q: 为什么这个高 AUC 的模型仍不能直接用于拍卖？
q_en: Why can't this high-AUC model be used directly in the auction?
why: 因为拍卖直接用 P(click) 算期望收益，概率必须被校准：P(click)=0.03 就得约 3% 真的点击。只排序对不够——AUC 高但概率偏，会系统性算错期望收益、定错价。校准是拍卖定价的硬要求。
why_en: The auction uses P(click) directly for expected revenue, so probabilities must be calibrated: P(click)=0.03 must mean ~3% actually click, not just correct ranking.
tradeoff: 校准概率（拍卖定价正确，但需额外校准步骤） vs 只优化排序 AUC（排序对但概率偏、定价错）
options: 因为 AUC 还不够高，只要把 AUC 再提上去就能直接用于拍卖
因为拍卖用 P(click) 算期望收益，概率必须校准，只排序对不够
因为模型体积太大，装不进拍卖服务器有限的内存里
因为拍卖只看排序不看概率，所以这个模型可以直接上线
options_en: Because AUC isn't high enough yet — push AUC up and it can go straight into the auction.
Because the auction computes expected revenue from P(click), so probabilities must be calibrated.
Because the model is too big to fit in the auction server's limited memory.
Because the auction only cares about ranking, not probability, so it can ship as-is.
whenOtherWins: 如果下游只需相对排序、不直接用概率数值（如纯 Top-K 推荐无定价），那排序 AUC 达标即可，校准不是硬要求。
whenOtherWins_en: If downstream needs only relative ranking and never the probability value (e.g. pure Top-K recommendation without pricing), ranking AUC suffices and calibration isn't mandatory.
optionExplanations: AUC 衡量排序，与概率是否准无关；再高的 AUC 也修不好偏离的概率。
对；GSP 拿 P(click) 直接定价，概率偏 6 倍会系统性算错期望收益，必须校准。
模型大小与校准无关，这里的问题是概率不准不是体积。
该拍卖恰恰直接用概率数值定价，说「只看排序」与场景矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: AUC measures ranking, unrelated to probability accuracy; higher AUC can't fix miscalibrated probabilities.
Correct — GSP prices directly from P(click), so a 6x-off probability systematically miscomputes expected revenue; calibration is required.
Model size is unrelated to calibration; the issue is inaccurate probability, not size.
This auction prices directly from the probability value, so 'ranking only' contradicts the scenario.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让预测概率与真实频率一致：预测 0.03 的样本约 3% 为正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration makes predicted probabilities match real frequencies: samples predicted 0.03 are positive ~3% of the time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告拍卖机制，用 P(click)×出价 算期望收益来排序定价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GSP (Generalized Second-Price auction) ranks and prices ads by P(click)×bid for expected revenue.

scenario: CTR 分布随时间漂移（新广告、节假日、热点），每天全量重训又太慢，跟不上非平稳变化。
scenario_en: CTR distribution drifts over time (new ads, holidays, trends); daily full retrains are too slow to track the non-stationary change.
q: 怎么让 LR 权重跟上非平稳漂移而不全量重训？
q_en: How do you keep LR weights tracking non-stationary drift without full retraining?
why: 用 FTRL 在线学习：新标注样本一到就增量更新权重，让模型持续适应非平稳漂移，不必全量重训。FTRL 还天然产出稀疏解，适合大规模 CTR。
why_en: Use FTRL online learning: ingest new labeled examples as they arrive and update weights incrementally, adapting to drift without a full retrain.
tradeoff: FTRL 在线（增量适应漂移+稀疏解，但需稳定的实时标注流） vs 全量重训（稳但慢、跟不上漂移）
options: 把全量重训频率从每天提到每小时，用更频繁的重训硬追漂移
用 FTRL 在线学习：新样本一到就增量更新权重
冻结权重不再更新，靠加大正则强度来抵抗漂移
每次检测到漂移就随机重置权重，从头再训一遍
options_en: Raise full retrains from daily to hourly and chase the drift by brute force.
Use FTRL online learning: update weights incrementally as new labels arrive.
Freeze the weights and resist drift by turning regularization up.
Randomly reset the weights and retrain from scratch each time drift shows up.
whenOtherWins: 如果分布基本平稳、无需实时适应，或实时标注流不可靠，定期全量重训反而更简单稳定。
whenOtherWins_en: If the distribution is largely stationary or the real-time label stream is unreliable, periodic full retraining is simpler and more stable.
optionExplanations: 更频繁全量重训成本高、仍有滞后，跟不上分钟级漂移，是在硬扛。
对；FTRL 增量吸收新标注、实时更新权重，正是为非平稳流设计，还给稀疏解。
冻结权重会让模型停在旧分布上，加正则也挡不住真实漂移。
随机重置丢掉已学到的信号，每次从零开始，代价巨大且不稳定。
optionExplanations_en: More frequent full retrains are costly and still lag, unable to track minute-scale drift — brute force.
Correct — FTRL absorbs new labels incrementally and updates weights in real time, built for non-stationary streams, and yields sparse solutions.
Freezing weights leaves the model on the old distribution; more regularization can't stop real drift.
Random reset discards learned signal and restarts from scratch — hugely costly and unstable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线学习算法，随新样本增量更新权重、产出稀疏解，适应非平稳漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTRL (Follow-The-Regularized-Leader) is an online-learning algorithm that updates weights incrementally, yields sparse solutions, and adapts to non-stationary drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据分布随时间持续变化，需模型持续适应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-stationary drift is a data distribution that keeps changing over time, requiring continuous adaptation.

scenario: 你要在 CTR 的 LR 里选正则方式：既想缩小服务模型体积，又想让在线更新稳定。
scenario_en: For CTR LR you pick regularization: shrink the serving model size and stabilize online updates.
q: L1 与 L2 正则在 LR 里分别解决什么？
q_en: What does L1 vs L2 regularization each solve in LR?
why: L1 把权重压成 0（稀疏化）→ 缩小服务体积；L2 收缩权重、稳定更新 → 抗过拟合/数值稳定。生产里常用 elastic net 把两者结合，既稀疏又稳定。
why_en: L1 zeros weights (sparsity) to shrink serving size, L2 shrinks and stabilizes updates; production often combines both via elastic net.
tradeoff: L1（稀疏、缩体积） vs L2（稳定、抗过拟合），elastic net 兼得
options: L1 和 L2 的效果完全相同，随便挑一个用都没差别
L1 置零权重换稀疏体积，L2 收缩权重换稳定更新
L1 会让模型变大、L2 会让模型变小，和通常的说法正好相反
两者都只影响训练速度，与模型体积和数值稳定性都无关
options_en: L1 and L2 do exactly the same thing; pick either one.
L1 zeros weights to buy sparsity and size; L2 shrinks weights to buy stable updates.
L1 makes the model bigger and L2 makes it smaller — the reverse of what people say.
Both only affect training speed and have nothing to do with size or numerical stability.
optionExplanations: 两者机制不同：L1 产稀疏、L2 只收缩，混为一谈会选错正则。
对；L1 缩体积、L2 稳更新，elastic net 结合两者，是生产标准做法。
L1 才缩体积（置零），说它让模型变大与事实相反。
L1/L2 直接影响稀疏性与稳定性，不是只管速度。
optionExplanations_en: Their mechanisms differ: L1 induces sparsity, L2 only shrinks; conflating them picks the wrong regularizer.
Correct — L1 shrinks size, L2 stabilizes updates, and elastic net combines them — the production standard.
L1 is what shrinks size (zeroing); saying it enlarges the model is backwards.
L1/L2 directly affect sparsity and stability, not just speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对权重平方惩罚，收缩权重、稳定更新、抗过拟合，但不产生稀疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L2 regularization penalizes squared weights, shrinking and stabilizing them and resisting overfit, but without sparsity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用 L1 与 L2 的正则组合，兼得稀疏与稳定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elastic net combines L1 and L2 regularization for both sparsity and stability.

scenario: 信用评分要满足 ECOA/GDPR：对每个决定给出可审计的逐特征理由。团队在 LR 与神经网络之间选。
scenario_en: Credit scoring must satisfy ECOA/GDPR: auditable per-feature reasons for each decision. The team chooses between LR and a neural net.
q: 为什么信用评分的可解释审计更偏 LR 而不是神经网络？
q_en: Why does auditable credit scoring favor LR over a neural net?
why: LR 的特征权重是直接、可审计的解释——每个特征对决定的贡献一目了然，满足 ECOA/GDPR 的信贷审计。神经网络的梯度型解释是事后近似，缺乏这种可审计性，监管通常不认。
why_en: LR's feature weights are direct, auditable explanations satisfying ECOA/GDPR, whereas neural gradient explanations are post-hoc approximations lacking that auditability.
tradeoff: LR 权重（直接可审计，满足监管） vs 神经梯度解释（事后近似、不可审计）
options: 神经网络的梯度归因更可审计，所以信贷评分反而更该用神经网络
LR 的特征权重是直接可审计的解释，满足 ECOA/GDPR
两者的可解释性其实相同，选哪个都能通过监管审计
信贷监管并不要求逐特征解释，挑精度最高的模型即可
options_en: Neural gradient attributions are more auditable, so credit scoring should prefer a neural net.
LR's feature weights are direct, auditable explanations that satisfy ECOA and GDPR.
The two are equally interpretable, so either one clears the audit.
Credit regulation never asks for per-feature reasons; just take the most accurate model.
optionExplanations: 神经梯度解释是近似、随输入不稳定，恰恰是监管难认的一类，说更可审计反了。
对；LR 权重直接给出每个特征的贡献，是监管认可的可审计解释。
两者可解释性差距明显，混为一谈会在信贷合规上踩坑。
ECOA/GDPR 明确要求对信贷决定给可审计理由，不能只看精度。
optionExplanations_en: Neural gradient explanations are approximate and input-unstable — exactly what regulators struggle to accept — so 'more auditable' is backwards.
Correct — LR weights directly give each feature's contribution, the regulator-accepted auditable explanation.
Their interpretability differs markedly; conflating them risks credit-compliance failure.
ECOA/GDPR explicitly require auditable reasons for credit decisions, so accuracy alone won't do.

termDefinitions.meaning: 美国信贷公平法，要求对信贷决定给出具体可审计理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ECOA (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) is a US fair-lending law requiring specific, auditable reasons for credit decisions.

scenario: CTR 数据是时间序列。有人想用标准 k-fold 交叉验证随机切分来评估模型。
scenario_en: CTR data is temporal. Someone wants standard random k-fold cross-validation to evaluate the model.
q: 时序数据上用标准 k-fold 有什么问题，该怎么做？
q_en: What's wrong with standard k-fold on temporal data, and what should you do?
why: 标准 k-fold 随机切分会把「未来」样本混进训练、泄漏未来信息，评估虚高、上线崩。时序数据要用基于时间的切分：训练第 1..N 天、验证第 N+1 天，严格保持时间顺序。
why_en: Random k-fold leaks future info by mixing later samples into training, inflating scores; use time-based splits (train days 1..N, validate day N+1).
tradeoff: 时间切分（无泄漏、贴合上线，但每折数据更少） vs 随机 k-fold（数据利用高但泄漏未来）
options: 没有问题，k-fold 随机切分对任何类型的数据都是最优做法
随机 k-fold 会泄漏未来、评估虚高；改用按时间切分
唯一的问题是 k-fold 太慢，减少折数就行，泄漏完全不用担心
时序数据根本无法离线验证，只能直接上线看线上效果
options_en: Nothing is wrong — random k-fold is the best split for any kind of data.
Random k-fold leaks the future and inflates scores; split by time instead.
The only issue is that k-fold is slow; use fewer folds and don't worry about leakage.
Temporal data cannot be validated offline at all; you just ship it and watch.
optionExplanations: 随机切分在时序上会泄漏未来，k-fold 并非对任何数据都最优。
对；时间切分保持「用过去预测未来」的因果顺序，避免未来泄漏，评估才可信。
问题是泄漏不是速度；减少折数不解决时间顺序被打乱的根因。
时序数据可用时间切分做严谨验证，说「只能上线看」是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Random splits leak the future on temporal data, so k-fold isn't optimal for everything.
Correct — time-based splits keep the causal 'past predicts future' order, avoiding leakage for trustworthy evaluation.
The issue is leakage, not speed; fewer folds doesn't fix the broken time order.
Temporal data can be rigorously validated with time-based splits; 'only ship and observe' is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间顺序划分训练/验证（训过去、验之后一天），防未来泄漏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-based split partitions train/validation by time (train the past, validate a later day), preventing future leakage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据随机分 K 折轮流做验证集；对时序数据会泄漏未来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: K-fold cross-validation randomly splits data into K folds used in turn for validation; it leaks the future on temporal data.

scenario: 表格排序特征很杂：tenure、设备、价格档、时间，彼此有非线性交互。你想不做大量手工交叉就把交互建进去。
scenario_en: Tabular ranking features are mixed: tenure, device, price bucket, time, with nonlinear interactions you'd rather not hand-cross.
q: GBDT 相对线性模型在建模交互上的核心优势是什么？
q_en: What's GBDT's core edge over linear models for modeling interactions?
why: GBDT 自动学习非线性与成对/高阶交互：树的每次分裂在特征上切一刀，层层嵌套就等于自动组合特征，不需要像 LR 那样手工做特征交叉。异构杂特征直接喂进去即可。
why_en: GBDT automatically learns nonlinear and pairwise/higher-order interactions via nested splits, without the manual feature crosses LR needs.
options: GBDT 比 LR 需要更多的手工特征交叉才能建出交互
树的嵌套分裂自动学非线性与高阶交互，无需手工交叉
GBDT 只能建线性关系，交互必须靠外部预处理来构造
GBDT 与 LR 同属线性模型，两者的交互建模能力完全相同
options_en: GBDT needs even more hand-built feature crosses than LR to capture interactions.
Nested splits learn nonlinear and higher-order interactions automatically, no manual crosses.
GBDT can only fit linear relationships; interactions must be built in preprocessing.
GBDT is a linear model just like LR, so the two capture interactions identically.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反：GBDT 自动学交互，省掉了 LR 需要的大量手工交叉。
对；嵌套分裂天然组合特征，非线性/高阶交互被自动捕捉，这是它对 LR 的核心优势。
GBDT 通过分裂建非线性和交互，不是只能线性。
GBDT 是非线性树模型，交互能力远强于线性 LR，不相同。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite: GBDT learns interactions automatically, sparing the many manual crosses LR needs.
Correct — nested splits naturally combine features, capturing nonlinear/higher-order interactions — its core edge over LR.
GBDT models nonlinearity and interactions through splits, not linear-only.
GBDT is a nonlinear tree model far stronger than linear LR on interactions — not identical.

termDefinitions.meaning: 三个及以上特征联合才体现的效应，GBDT 靠嵌套分裂自动捕捉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A higher-order interaction is an effect only appearing when three or more features combine, which GBDT captures via nested splits.

scenario: 你要说清为什么 GBDT 在杂乱的真实表格数据上如此好用。
scenario_en: You explain why GBDT is so effective on messy real-world tabular data.
q: GBDT 的架构性强项有哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are GBDT's architectural strengths? (multiple)
why: 四大强项：为缺失值学默认分裂方向（不引入填充偏差）；类别/数值/序数异构特征原生共存；按分裂增益给内置特征重要性；对单调变换不变→对离群值鲁棒。这些让脏表格几乎免预处理。
why_en: GBDT learns default split directions for missing values, natively mixes heterogeneous feature types, gives built-in feature importance, and is outlier-robust (invariant to monotonic transforms).
options: 为缺失值学习默认分裂方向，无需填充、不引入填充偏差
类别/数值/序数异构特征原生共存，无需重预处理
按分裂增益给出内置特征重要性
对离群值鲁棒（分裂对单调变换不变）
能直接处理原始图像像素，无需卷积
options_en: Learns default split directions for missing values — no imputation, no imputation bias.
Heterogeneous categorical/numeric/ordinal features coexist natively, no heavy preprocessing.
Built-in feature importance from split gain.
Outlier-robust (splits invariant to monotonic transforms).
Handles raw image pixels directly, no convolution needed.
optionExplanations: 对；缺失值当作可分裂方向来学，避开了均值/中位填充的偏差。
对；异构类型无需统一编码即可共存，是脏表格的福音。
对；分裂增益天然给出特征重要性，辅助解释与选择。
对；基于排序的分裂对单调变换不变，天然抗离群。
错；GBDT 吃的是表格特征，学不了原始像素的空间层级，那是 CNN 的活。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — missing values become a learnable split direction, avoiding mean/median imputation bias.
Correct — heterogeneous types coexist without unified encoding — a boon for messy tables.
Correct — split gain naturally yields feature importance, aiding interpretation and selection.
Correct — rank-based splits are invariant to monotonic transforms, naturally outlier-robust.
Wrong — GBDT consumes tabular features and can't learn spatial hierarchies from raw pixels — that's a CNN's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保持大小顺序的变换（如取对数）；GBDT 的分裂对其不变，故抗离群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A monotonic transform preserves order (e.g. log); GBDT's splits are invariant to it, giving outlier robustness.

scenario: 真实表格里很多列有缺失值。有人主张先用均值填充再喂给 GBDT。
scenario_en: Many real-world columns have missing values; someone proposes mean-imputing before feeding GBDT.
q: GBDT 怎么处理缺失值，为什么通常不需要手工填充？
q_en: How does GBDT handle missing values, and why is manual imputation usually unneeded?
why: GBDT 在每个分裂点为缺失样本学一个默认走向（往左还是往右），让缺失本身携带信息、且不引入填充偏差。均值填充反而把「缺失」抹成一个虚假的具体值，可能扭曲分布。
why_en: GBDT learns a default split direction for missing samples at each node, letting missingness carry signal without imputation bias, whereas mean-filling injects a fake value.
tradeoff: GBDT 学默认方向（保留缺失信息、无填充偏差） vs 均值填充（抹平缺失、引入虚假值）
options: GBDT 无法处理缺失值，必须先做均值或中位数填充
在每个分裂点为缺失样本学一个默认走向，缺失自带信息
GBDT 会自动丢弃所有含缺失值的样本行再训练
GBDT 把缺失值一律当成 0 参与分裂点的比较
options_en: GBDT can't handle missing values; you must mean- or median-impute first.
It learns a default direction for missing rows at each split, so missingness itself carries signal.
GBDT silently drops every row that contains a missing value before training.
GBDT treats every missing value as 0 when comparing against a split threshold.
optionExplanations: GBDT 原生支持缺失值，强制先填充反而丢掉「缺失」这个信号。
对；学默认分裂方向让缺失参与建模，避开均值填充带来的偏差。
GBDT 不会删行，缺失样本照样参与分裂、走默认方向。
一律当 0 是错误假设，GBDT 是学一个方向，不是硬编成 0。
optionExplanations_en: GBDT natively supports missing values; forcing imputation discards the 'missingness' signal.
Correct — learning a default split direction lets missingness inform the model, avoiding mean-imputation bias.
GBDT doesn't drop rows; missing samples still split via the default direction.
Treating all as 0 is a wrong assumption; GBDT learns a direction, not a hard-coded 0.

termDefinitions.term: default split direction / 默认分裂方向
termDefinitions.meaning: GBDT 为缺失值在每个分裂点学的走向（左/右），使缺失本身可建模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A default split direction is the left/right route GBDT learns for missing values at each node, making missingness modelable.

scenario: 你要在 XGBoost 与 LightGBM 之间做选择，两者树生长策略不同。
scenario_en: You choose between XGBoost and LightGBM, whose tree-growth strategies differ.
q: XGBoost 与 LightGBM 的树生长方式有何不同，各偏向什么？
q_en: How do XGBoost and LightGBM grow trees, and what does each favor?
why: XGBoost 按层生长（level-wise，树更平衡、更不易过拟合）；LightGBM 按叶生长（leaf-wise，每次分裂损失下降最大的叶，更快、大数据上更好，但小数据要调 max_depth 防过拟合）。
why_en: XGBoost grows level-wise (balanced, less overfit), LightGBM grows leaf-wise (splits the highest-loss-reduction leaf — faster, better on big data, but tune max_depth to avoid overfit on small data).
tradeoff: XGBoost level-wise（平衡、抗过拟合，稍慢） vs LightGBM leaf-wise（快、大数据强，小数据易过拟合）
options: 两者树的生长方式完全相同，只是实现和名字不一样
XGBoost 按层生长更平衡；LightGBM 按叶生长更快
XGBoost 是 leaf-wise、LightGBM 是 level-wise，正好相反
两者都不长树，本质上都是加了正则的线性模型
options_en: They grow trees identically and differ only in implementation and name.
XGBoost grows level-wise and stays balanced; LightGBM grows leaf-wise and is faster.
XGBoost is leaf-wise and LightGBM is level-wise — exactly the other way around.
Neither one grows trees; both are really regularized linear models.
optionExplanations: 生长策略正是两者的核心区别，说相同抹掉了选型依据。
对；按层 vs 按叶决定了平衡性/速度/过拟合风险，是选型的关键。
方向反了：XGBoost 才 level-wise、LightGBM 才 leaf-wise。
两者都是树模型（GBDT），不是线性模型。
optionExplanations_en: Growth strategy is their core difference; 'the same' erases the basis for choosing.
Correct — level-wise vs leaf-wise sets balance/speed/overfit risk — the key to selection.
Reversed: XGBoost is level-wise and LightGBM is leaf-wise.
Both are tree models (GBDT), not linear.

termDefinitions.meaning: XGBoost 逐层扩展所有节点，树更平衡、更抗过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Level-wise growth (XGBoost) expands all nodes layer by layer, giving balanced, less-overfit trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: LightGBM 每次分裂损失下降最大的叶，更快但小数据易过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leaf-wise growth (LightGBM) splits the leaf with the largest loss reduction — faster but overfit-prone on small data.

scenario: 任务 A：几千万行训练数据，训练速度是瓶颈。任务 B：几万行小数据、过拟合风险高。
scenario_en: Task A: tens of millions of rows where training speed is the bottleneck. Task B: tens of thousands of rows with high overfit risk.
q: 这两个任务分别更适合 XGBoost 还是 LightGBM？
q_en: Which of XGBoost vs LightGBM fits each task?
why: 大数据（>几百万行）选 LightGBM——leaf-wise 训练更快；小数据/高过拟合风险选 XGBoost——level-wise 更平衡、更抗过拟合。别一句「我用 XGBoost」了事，要按数据规模和过拟合风险分场景选。
why_en: For big data (>few million rows) pick LightGBM (faster leaf-wise training); for small/overfit-prone data pick XGBoost (balanced level-wise).
tradeoff: LightGBM（大数据训练快，小数据易过拟合） vs XGBoost（抗过拟合，大数据略慢）
options: 两个任务都统一用 XGBoost，数据规模不该影响框架的选择
A（大数据）用 LightGBM；B（小数据）用 XGBoost 抗过拟合
两个任务都用 LightGBM，小数据上也完全不必担心过拟合这件事
按字母顺序选，X 排在 L 前面所以两个任务都统一用 XGBoost
options_en: Use XGBoost for both tasks; data size should not drive the framework choice.
Task A (big data) takes LightGBM; task B (small data) takes XGBoost for overfit resistance.
Use LightGBM for both — even on small data overfitting is nothing to worry about.
Choose alphabetically: X comes before L, so both tasks get XGBoost.
whenOtherWins: 若小数据但已通过限制 max_depth/叶数严格约束了 LightGBM，也可用它换取更快训练；反之大数据但强调稳健也可用 XGBoost。
whenOtherWins_en: On small data you can still use LightGBM if you tightly cap max_depth/leaves; conversely on big data you can use XGBoost when robustness matters most.
optionExplanations: 无脑 XGBoost 忽略了大数据下 LightGBM 的训练速度优势。
对；按数据规模与过拟合风险分场景，这正是「别只说用 XGBoost」的意思。
小数据用 leaf-wise 的 LightGBM 恰恰更易过拟合，需要格外调 max_depth。
按字母选是无稽之谈，选型要看数据规模和过拟合风险。
optionExplanations_en: Blindly using XGBoost ignores LightGBM's training-speed edge on big data.
Correct — split by data size and overfit risk — exactly the 'don't just say XGBoost' point.
Leaf-wise LightGBM on small data is more overfit-prone, needing careful max_depth tuning.
Alphabetical choice is nonsense; select by data size and overfit risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 树的最大深度，限制它可抑制 leaf-wise 生长在小数据上的过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: max_depth caps tree depth; limiting it curbs leaf-wise overfitting on small data.

scenario: 你要调一个 GBDT，面试官问你按什么顺序调超参最有效。
scenario_en: You tune a GBDT and the interviewer asks the most effective order of hyperparameters.
q: 把 GBDT 的调参优先级排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order GBDT hyperparameter tuning by priority:
steps: 先定 learning rate + n_estimators（控制 bias-variance 主轴）
再调 max_depth（控制单树复杂度）
最后调行/列 subsampling（提升泛化、抗过拟合）
why: 优先级：学习率×树数（bias-variance 主旋钮）先定，再调 max_depth（复杂度），最后行列采样（泛化）。先把最影响拟合能力的旋钮定好，再逐层收细，顺序反了会在错误的容量下瞎调。
why_en: Tune learning rate + n_estimators (the bias-variance axis) first, then max_depth (complexity), then row/column subsampling (generalization).
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["learning rate + n_estimators"] --> B["max_depth 复杂度"]
  B --> C["行/列 subsampling 泛化"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 步长与树数，共同决定 bias-variance；小步长需更多树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning rate (step size) and n_estimators (number of trees) jointly set bias-variance; a smaller rate needs more trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每棵树随机用部分行/列训练，提升泛化、抑制过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Subsampling trains each tree on a random subset of rows/columns to improve generalization and curb overfit.

scenario: 三个任务：(A) 二分类要看整体判别力；(B) 搜索排序要重视排在最前的结果；(C) 欺诈检测正负极不平衡。
scenario_en: Three tasks: (A) binary classification needing overall discrimination; (B) search ranking weighting top results; (C) fraud detection with severe class imbalance.
q: 这三类任务分别该用什么评估指标？
q_en: Which metric fits each of these three tasks?
why: 二分类整体判别→ROC-AUC；排序且重视 Top→NDCG（给靠前位置更高权重）；不平衡欺诈→F1（兼顾精确率与召回，不被多数类淹没）。指标必须匹配任务的成功定义，用错会优化偏方向。
why_en: ROC-AUC for binary discrimination, NDCG for ranking that weights top items, and F1 for imbalanced fraud — the metric must match the task's success definition.
tradeoff: ROC-AUC（整体判别） vs NDCG（重视 Top 排序） vs F1（抗不平衡）
options: 三个任务统一都用准确率 accuracy，简单、便于横向对比和汇报
A 用 ROC-AUC、B 用 NDCG 重 Top、C 用 F1 抗不平衡
三个都用 NDCG，反正任何任务最后都能转成一个排序问题
三个都用 F1，它兼顾精确率和召回，其它指标其实都没什么用
options_en: Use plain accuracy for all three — simple, and easy to compare and report.
A: ROC-AUC; B: NDCG for top-weighted ranking; C: F1 for imbalance.
Use NDCG for all three, since any task can be recast as a ranking problem.
Use F1 for all three; it balances precision and recall and the rest are useless.
whenOtherWins: 若不平衡任务更在意「抓住尽量多的欺诈」，可改看召回率或 PR-AUC；指标随业务对精确/召回的偏好而变。
whenOtherWins_en: If the imbalanced task prioritizes catching as much fraud as possible, switch to recall or PR-AUC; the metric shifts with the precision/recall priority.
optionExplanations: 准确率在不平衡欺诈下会被多数类淹没（全判非欺诈也高分），三任务统一用它会误导。
对；AUC 看整体判别、NDCG 重 Top、F1 抗不平衡，各自匹配任务的成功定义。
NDCG 是排序指标，用在二分类整体判别或不平衡欺诈上不对口。
F1 适合不平衡，但排序任务用它丢掉了位置权重，一刀切不合适。
optionExplanations_en: Accuracy is drowned by the majority class in imbalanced fraud (predict all non-fraud scores high), so using it for all misleads.
Correct — AUC for discrimination, NDCG for top-weighting, F1 for imbalance — each matches the task's success definition.
NDCG is a ranking metric, mismatched for binary discrimination or imbalanced fraud.
F1 suits imbalance, but on ranking it drops positional weighting — one-size-fits-all is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序质量指标，给靠前位置更高权重，衡量把相关项排在前面的程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a ranking metric weighting top positions more, measuring how well relevant items are ranked high.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确率与召回率的调和平均，适合类别不平衡（如欺诈）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, suited to class imbalance like fraud.

scenario: 你要总结「什么时候经典 ML 会打败神经网络」的复现场景。
scenario_en: You summarize the recurring scenarios where classical ML beats neural nets.
q: 哪些复现场景下经典 ML 会胜过神经网络？(多选)
q_en: In which recurring scenarios does classical ML beat neural nets? (multiple)
why: 四类：需逐特征可解释、数据量 <100K 表格、sub-5ms 严延迟、监管要确定性可审计。这些约束下经典模型直接达标，DNN 要么过拟合要么不可审计。
why_en: Four cases: per-feature interpretability, under 100K tabular rows, sub-5ms latency, and deterministic auditability — classical models clear all four while a DNN either overfits or cannot be audited.
options: 需要逐特征可解释（ECOA/GDPR，LR 权重 + GBDT SHAP 原生）
低数据量（<100K 表格样本，DNN 易过拟合）
严格延迟（sub-5ms 广告竞价，LR 在 CPU 上无 GPU 复杂度）
监管合规需确定性可审计（经典模型 run-to-run 一致，随机网络不确定）
输入是原始视频流、需要学习时空表示
options_en: Per-feature interpretability needed (ECOA/GDPR; LR weights + GBDT SHAP native).
Low data volume (<100K tabular; DNNs overfit).
Strict latency (sub-5ms ad bidding; LR on CPU, no GPU complexity).
Regulatory compliance needing deterministic auditability (classical is run-to-run identical; stochastic nets aren't).
Input is raw video needing learned spatiotemporal representations.
optionExplanations: 对；可解释是经典模型的主场，LR 权重与 GBDT SHAP 原生满足监管。
对；<100K 表格上 GBDT 稳胜 DNN（后者过拟合、需重正则）。
对；sub-5ms 竞价下 LR 的 CPU 亚毫秒推理直接达标，省掉 GPU。
对；确定性可审计是经典强项，dropout/随机网络 run-to-run 不一致。
错；原始视频的时空表示正是神经网络（非结构化模态）的主场，不是经典 ML。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — interpretability is classical's home turf; LR weights and GBDT SHAP natively satisfy regulators.
Correct — on <100K tabular, GBDT reliably beats DNNs (which overfit and need heavy regularization).
Correct — under sub-5ms bidding, LR's sub-ms CPU inference meets the bar and skips GPU.
Correct — deterministic auditability is classical's strength; dropout/stochastic nets aren't run-to-run identical.
Wrong — raw-video spatiotemporal representation is a neural (unstructured-modality) job, not classical ML.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同输入同参数每次输出一致；经典模型满足，含 dropout 的随机网络不满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Run-to-run determinism means identical outputs for identical inputs/params each run; classical models satisfy it, stochastic nets with dropout don't.

tradeoff: 可解释性/确定性/延迟 vs 模型容量与精度上限

scenario: 表格任务只有约 8 万条标注样本，团队想上一个深度网络提精度。
scenario_en: A tabular task has only ~80K labeled samples; the team wants a deep net for accuracy.
q: 8 万条表格数据，该选 GBDT 还是 DNN？
q_en: With 80K tabular rows, GBDT or DNN?
why: 选 GBDT：在 <100K 的表格数据上 GBDT 通常胜过 DNN——DNN 数据不够会过拟合、要重正则和大量调参。数据量不到百万级时，深度网络的容量优势发挥不出来，反成负担。
why_en: GBDT: on <100K tabular rows it usually beats a DNN, which overfits without millions of samples and needs heavy regularization.
tradeoff: GBDT（小数据稳、少调参） vs DNN（<100K 易过拟合、需重正则）
options: DNN：数据少反而更该上深度网络，靠模型结构补数据不足
GBDT：<100K 表格上通常胜过 DNN（后者数据不足会过拟合）
LLM：把这 8 万行表格拼成文本喂进去做 few-shot 预测
两者效果一样，随便选一个，数据量不影响最终结果
options_en: A DNN — with little data you need depth, and structure makes up for the missing rows.
GBDT: on under 100K tabular rows it usually beats a DNN, which overfits on too little data.
An LLM: flatten the 80K rows into text and few-shot it.
They perform the same; pick either, data volume changes nothing.
whenOtherWins: 当标注涨到百万级、或核心信号来自非结构化模态时，DNN 才反超 GBDT。
whenOtherWins_en: A DNN overtakes GBDT only once labels reach millions or the core signal is unstructured.
optionExplanations: 数据越少 DNN 越容易过拟合，「靠结构补数据」在 8 万级表格上站不住。
对；<100K 表格是 GBDT 的稳赢区，少过拟合、少调参、精度更好。
8 万条数值表格塞进 LLM 又慢又贵、丢精度，明显错配。
数据量恰恰决定 GBDT/DNN 的胜负，说无影响会选错。
optionExplanations_en: Less data makes a DNN overfit more; 'structure compensates' doesn't hold on 80K tabular rows.
Correct — <100K tabular is GBDT's reliable-win zone: less overfit, less tuning, better accuracy.
Stuffing 80K numeric rows into an LLM is slow, costly, and loses precision — a clear mismatch.
Data volume decides GBDT vs DNN; 'no effect' leads to the wrong pick.

termDefinitions.term: data volume threshold / 数据量门槛
termDefinitions.meaning: DNN 稳胜 GBDT 大约需百万级标注；<100K 表格 GBDT 更优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data-volume threshold: a DNN reliably beats GBDT around millions of labels; below 100K tabular, GBDT wins.

scenario: 医疗/金融合规要求：同样输入每次必须给出完全相同、可审计的输出。有人提议用带 dropout 的深度网络。
scenario_en: Healthcare/finance compliance requires identical, auditable output for identical input every run. Someone proposes a dropout-based deep net.
q: 确定性可审计的合规约束下，为什么偏经典模型？
q_en: Under a deterministic-auditability constraint, why favor classical models?
why: 经典模型 run-to-run 完全一致、可审计；而含 dropout 等随机成分的网络每次输出可能不同，破坏确定性与可复现的审计。合规硬要求确定性时，LR/GBDT 直接满足，随机网络出局。
why_en: Classical models are run-to-run identical and auditable, while dropout/stochastic nets can differ per run, breaking determinism required by compliance.
tradeoff: 经典模型（确定、可审计、可复现） vs 随机网络（精度或高但 run-to-run 不一致）
options: 含 dropout 的随机网络输出更确定，因此在合规审计场景反而更合适
经典模型 run-to-run 完全一致、可审计；随机网络每次可能不同
合规审计并不在乎确定性，选精度最高的那个模型即可
只要把网络参数加密存储，就等于满足了确定性审计要求
options_en: Networks with dropout are more deterministic, so they actually fit compliance audits better.
Classical models are run-to-run identical and auditable; stochastic nets can differ every run.
Compliance audits don't care about determinism; just take the most accurate model.
Encrypting the network weights is enough to satisfy a deterministic-audit requirement.
optionExplanations: 含 dropout 的网络恰恰不确定，说它更确定与事实相反。
对；确定性+可审计是硬约束，经典模型天然满足，随机网络破坏可复现审计。
医疗/金融明确要求确定性可审计，不能只看精度。
加密保护的是数据机密，不改变模型输出是否 run-to-run 一致，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Dropout nets are precisely non-deterministic, so 'more deterministic' is backwards.
Correct — determinism + auditability is a hard constraint that classical models meet natively, while stochastic nets break reproducible audit.
Healthcare/finance explicitly require deterministic auditability, so accuracy alone won't do.
Encryption protects confidentiality, not whether outputs are run-to-run identical — off point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练/推理时随机丢弃部分神经元的正则手段，会引入输出随机性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dropout randomly drops neurons as regularization, introducing output randomness.

scenario: 任务：约 5 万条标注交易 + 严格可解释要求（监管）+ 5ms 延迟 SLA。
scenario_en: Task: ~50K labeled transactions + strict interpretability (regulatory) + a 5ms latency SLA.
q: 同时满足小数据、可解释、5ms 的最佳选择是？
q_en: What best satisfies small data, interpretability, and 5ms at once?
why: 选 LightGBM + SHAP：5 万条表格是 GBDT 的稳赢区，GBDT 毫秒级推理满足 5ms SLA，SHAP 提供逐预测可审计归因满足监管。三条硬约束一次全中，DNN/LLM 在数据量和可解释上都不合。
why_en: LightGBM + SHAP: 50K tabular is GBDT's win zone, its millisecond inference meets 5ms, and SHAP gives auditable per-prediction attribution — all three constraints at once.
tradeoff: LightGBM+SHAP（小数据准+毫秒+可审计） vs DNN/LLM（数据不足过拟合、黑箱、延迟高）
options: 深度神经网络 + 事后梯度归因，靠大容量同时满足这三条约束
LightGBM + SHAP：小数据稳赢、毫秒级、逐预测可审计
LLM few-shot，省掉标注成本和整条特征工程管线
纯逻辑回归，忽略交易特征之间的非线性交互
options_en: A deep net plus post-hoc gradient attribution, using capacity to cover all three constraints.
LightGBM + SHAP: wins on small tabular, runs in milliseconds, gives auditable per-prediction reasons.
A few-shot LLM, skipping labeling cost and the whole feature pipeline.
Plain logistic regression, ignoring nonlinear interactions between transaction features.
whenOtherWins: 若数据涨到百万级、可解释不再是硬约束、且延迟预算放宽，DNN 才可能反超。
whenOtherWins_en: Only if data grows to millions, interpretability is no longer required, and the latency budget loosens would a DNN overtake.
optionExplanations: 5 万条上 DNN 会过拟合，事后梯度解释也不满足监管可审计，两头不讨好。
对；LightGBM 的表格精度+毫秒延迟+SHAP 可审计，正好三约束全中。
标注其实充足（5 万），LLM few-shot 又慢又贵、还违反 5ms，浪费标签。
纯 LR 抓不住交易特征的非线性交互，欺诈上通常欠拟合、精度不如 GBDT。
optionExplanations_en: A DNN overfits on 50K, and post-hoc gradient explanations fail regulatory auditability — losing on both.
Correct — LightGBM's tabular accuracy + millisecond latency + SHAP auditability hits all three constraints.
Labels are actually ample (50K); a few-shot LLM is slow, costly, and breaks 5ms — wasting labels.
Plain LR misses nonlinear interactions among transaction features, usually underfitting fraud versus GBDT.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每次预测按特征分配贡献的可解释方法，满足监管逐决定审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attributes each prediction to features, satisfying per-decision regulatory audit.

scenario: 系统最终要上神经网络，但团队已有成熟的经典模型。面试官问经典模型在神经栈里还能扮演什么角色。
scenario_en: The system will go neural, but the team has mature classical models. The interviewer asks what role classical still plays in a neural stack.
q: 在神经系统里，LR 和 GBDT 还能扮演什么角色？
q_en: In a neural system, what roles can LR and GBDT still play?
why: LR 可作神经输出的校准层，GBDT 可作 embedding 层前的特征选择器。经典模型不必被抛弃，而是与神经栈互补。
why_en: LR can sit on top as a calibration layer for neural outputs and GBDT can select features ahead of the embedding layers, so classical models complement the neural stack instead of being thrown away.
options: 神经网络一上线，经典模型就必须彻底废弃，不再有任何角色
LR 做输出校准层，GBDT 做 embedding 前的特征选择器
经典模型只能当训练数据的清洗工具，不进入推理路径
LR/GBDT 只能替神经网络背锅，不参与任何有用的环节
options_en: Once the neural net ships, classical models must be retired completely with no role left.
LR becomes a calibration layer on the outputs; GBDT a feature selector before the embeddings.
Classical models can only scrub training data and never enter the inference path.
LR and GBDT only take the blame for the neural net and do nothing useful.
optionExplanations: 经典模型可与神经栈互补，说必须废弃是非黑即白的误解。
对；LR 校准 + GBDT 选特征，是经典模型在神经系统里的实用角色。
经典模型能进推理路径（如输出校准层），不止是离线清洗工具。
「背锅」不是技术角色，LR/GBDT 有校准/选特征等实打实的用途。
optionExplanations_en: Classical models complement the neural stack; 'must be discarded' is a black-and-white misread.
Correct — LR for calibration and GBDT for feature selection are practical classical roles in a neural system.
Classical models can enter the inference path (e.g. an output calibration layer), not just offline cleaning.
'Taking blame' isn't a technical role; LR/GBDT have real uses like calibration and feature selection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接在模型输出后、把分数校准成真实概率的一层（常用 LR）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration layer sits after a model's output to map scores into true probabilities, often via LR.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用 GBDT 的特征重要性筛出有用特征，再喂给下游 embedding 层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature selector uses GBDT feature importance to pick useful features before a downstream embedding layer.

scenario: 经典模型在表格/延迟/可解释场景一路够用，但系统要开始从几十亿候选里做语义检索，且引入图像/文本原始输入。
scenario_en: Classical models suffice on tabular/latency/interpretability, but the system must now do semantic retrieval over billions of candidates with raw image/text inputs.
q: 经典 ML 的天花板出现在什么时候，之后升级到什么？
q_en: When does classical ML hit its ceiling, and what comes next?
why: 天花板出现在：输入变成非结构化（图像/文本/序列），或系统需要学习共享 embedding 表示来做检索。此时经典模型的手工特征吃不下原始信号，要升级到 two-tower / Wide&Deep / DCN 这类神经架构。
why_en: The ceiling appears with unstructured input or when the system needs learned shared-embedding representations for retrieval, escalating to two-tower / Wide&Deep / DCN.
tradeoff: 经典（表格/延迟/可解释强，但吃不了非结构化/共享 embedding） vs 神经（两塔/W&D/DCN 补上表示学习）
options: 经典模型没有天花板，任何任务加加特征都够用，永远不需要升级架构
输入变非结构化或需共享 embedding；升级到 two-tower/DCN
天花板只在数据量太小的时候出现，多喂一些数据就行，不用换架构
天花板在 QPS 太高时出现，换更大的 CPU 机型或多加副本就能解决
options_en: Classical models have no ceiling; add a few features and they cover any task, forever.
The ceiling is unstructured input or needing shared embeddings; move to two-tower or DCN.
The ceiling only shows up when data is too small — feed it more data, keep the architecture.
The ceiling shows up when QPS gets too high; a bigger CPU machine or more replicas fixes it.
optionExplanations: 经典模型确有天花板：原始像素/文本和共享 embedding 检索它做不了。
对；非结构化输入或共享 embedding 检索是升级到神经架构（两塔/W&D/DCN）的信号。
天花板不是数据量问题，而是模态与表示需求，加数据补不上。
高 QPS 时经典模型反而更合适（更快），不是它的天花板。
optionExplanations_en: Classical models do have a ceiling: raw pixels/text and shared-embedding retrieval are beyond them.
Correct — unstructured input or shared-embedding retrieval is the signal to escalate to neural (two-tower/W&D/DCN).
The ceiling isn't a data-volume issue but modality and representation needs; more data won't help.
At high QPS classical is actually more suitable (faster), not its ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动做特征交叉的神经排序架构，从 Wide&Deep 演进而来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep & Cross Network) is a neural ranking architecture that automates feature crossing, evolved from Wide & Deep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户与物品映射到同一隐空间的稠密向量，支撑相似度检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared embedding maps users and items into one latent space of dense vectors to support similarity retrieval.

q: 补全用经典模型辩护的「三段式公式」：
q_en: Fill in the three-part formula for defending a classical model.
text: 辩护公式：先点名 {{constraint}}（约束，如 5ms SLA）→ 再点名 {{model}}（模型，如 LR on CPU）→ 最后 {{quantify}}（量化，如 0.1ms 推理只占 2% 预算）。
text_en: Defense formula: name the {{constraint}} (e.g. 5ms SLA) → name the {{model}} (e.g. LR on CPU) → {{quantify}} (e.g. 0.1ms inference uses 2% of budget).
why: 记忆钩子：约束→模型→量化。面试里每个选择都用这三步说清，比空喊「LR 更快」有说服力得多。
why_en: Memory hook: constraint → model → quantify — defending each choice this way beats vaguely claiming 'LR is faster.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 用具体数字（延迟 ms、模型 KB、预算占比）支撑取舍，而非空泛形容词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To quantify is to back a trade-off with concrete numbers (latency ms, model KB, budget share) instead of vague adjectives.

scenario: 表格里价格特征有极端离群值（个别订单金额是正常值的上千倍），团队担心它扭曲模型。
scenario_en: A price feature has extreme outliers (a few orders thousands of times the norm); the team worries it distorts the model.
q: 为什么 GBDT 对这种离群值相对鲁棒？
q_en: Why is GBDT relatively robust to such outliers?
why: GBDT 的分裂基于特征的排序/阈值，而非绝对数值，对单调变换不变——离群值只是「排在最右」，不会像线性模型那样按数值大小成比例拉扯参数。所以极端值对树分裂影响有限。
why_en: GBDT splits on feature order/thresholds, not absolute magnitude, so it's invariant to monotonic transforms and an outlier is just 'ranked far right,' not scaling parameters.
tradeoff: GBDT（基于排序阈值、抗离群） vs 线性模型（按数值成比例、易被离群拉扯）
options: 因为 GBDT 训练时会自动检测并删掉这些离群样本
因为分裂基于排序/阈值、对单调变换不变，不按数值拉扯参数
因为 GBDT 会把所有特征强制归一化到 0-1 区间再分裂
因为离群值对任何模型都没有影响，本来就不需要担心
options_en: Because GBDT automatically detects and deletes outlier rows during training.
Because splits use order and thresholds, invariant to monotonic transforms, so magnitude never drags parameters.
Because GBDT force-normalizes every feature into 0-1 before splitting.
Because outliers have no effect on any model, so there was never anything to worry about.
whenOtherWins: 若离群值本身是有意义的强信号（如欺诈的异常大额），保留它反而有用；鲁棒不等于要抹掉它。
whenOtherWins_en: If the outlier is itself a meaningful strong signal (e.g. an abnormally large fraudulent amount), keeping it helps; robustness doesn't mean erasing it.
optionExplanations: GBDT 不删离群值，它是靠排序分裂让离群值影响有限，而非丢弃数据。
对；分裂看排序不看绝对值，离群值不会像线性模型那样按数值比例扭曲参数。
GBDT 不需要归一化，树对特征尺度本就不敏感，这不是它抗离群的原因。
离群值对线性模型影响很大，说「对任何模型都无影响」是错的。
optionExplanations_en: GBDT doesn't delete outliers; rank-based splits limit their influence rather than discarding data.
Correct — splits use order not magnitude, so an outlier doesn't distort parameters proportionally as in a linear model.
GBDT needs no normalization and is scale-insensitive; that's not why it resists outliers.
Outliers strongly affect linear models, so 'no effect on any model' is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 极端值不会成比例扭曲模型；GBDT 因基于排序分裂而具备。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Outlier robustness means extreme values don't proportionally distort the model; GBDT has it via rank-based splits.

scenario: 面试官质疑：LR 这么简单，工业界真的还在用吗，是不是早被深度模型取代了？
scenario_en: The interviewer challenges: LR is so simple — does industry really still use it, or has deep learning replaced it?
q: 关于「良好工程化的 LR」，有什么经典证据支撑它仍在大规模生产？
q_en: What classic evidence supports well-engineered LR still running in large-scale production?
why: Google 2013 年的广告点击论文表明：良好工程化的 LR（配合特征交叉、FTRL 在线学习、校准）能匹敌复杂替代方案。工业界至今在 CTR 上大规模用它，是因为它在延迟/成本/可解释上的综合优势，而非精度最高。
why_en: Google's 2013 ad-click paper showed well-engineered LR matches complex alternatives, and it's still used at scale for CTR due to latency/cost/interpretability advantages.
options: LR 早已被深度模型全面取代，工业界现在已经完全不再使用它
Google 2013 广告点击论文：工程化良好的 LR 可匹敌复杂替代
LR 只出现在学生作业和教科书里，从未进过真实的生产系统
LR 仅用于图像分类，且精度低于所有神经网络方案，早已淘汰
options_en: LR was fully superseded by deep models long ago and industry no longer uses it at all.
Google's 2013 ad-click paper: a well-engineered LR matches far more complex alternatives.
